title: Balance Point

concept.title: Left sum and right sum from one total
body: To compare the sum on the left of a position with the sum on the right, you do not need to add them up again for every position. Compute the **total** once. While walking from the left, keep the sum of everything before the current element; the sum after it is `total - left - a[i]`.
Updating `left` after the check keeps the current element out of both sides. This turns a quadratic search into one pass.

statement: Find the smallest index `i` (counting from 0) such that the sum of the elements to the left of `i` equals the sum of the elements to the right of `i`. The element at `i` itself is in neither sum, and an empty side has sum 0. If there is no such index, print -1.

examples.note: At index 3 the left sum is 1+7+3 = 11 and the right sum is 5+6 = 11.

hints: First compute the sum of the whole array.
While walking, keep `left`, the sum of the elements before the current one.
The right sum is `total - left - a[i]`.

explanation: Compute the total once. At each index the right sum is the total minus the left sum minus the element, so each index is checked in O(1).

code.python:
import sys
input = sys.stdin.readline

n = int(input())
a = list(map(int, input().split()))

total = sum(a)
left = 0
answer = -1
for i in range(n):
    if left == total - left - a[i]:
        answer = i
        break
    left += a[i]
print(answer)
